prerequisites: No prior requirements for the course.
It is recommended to have studied Chemistry in high school and have basic knowledge of organic and inorganic chemical nomenclature and common magnitudes and units in Physics and Chemistry.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can transmit information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Adopt a responsible, orderly attitude at work and willingness to learn considering the challenge of continuous training.

Apply the strategies of the scientific methodology: analyze the problematic situation qualitatively and quantitatively, propose hypotheses and solutions using models typical of industrial engineering.
Work effectively in groups integrating capabilities and knowledge to make decisions in the field of industrial engineering.
Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.
Communicates and transmits knowledge, procedures, skills and results using engineering and specific chemical terminology.
Has acquired knowledge and learning strategies that allow progression in subsequent studies.

Applies the strategies of the scientific method to solve problems related to the properties and behavior of matter in different applications, analyzes the problematic situation with awareness of the theoretical framework that guides it, makes decisions with initiative and creativity, uses the appropriate equations and models for its resolution.
Works effectively in groups during the development and achievement of laboratory experiments integrating capabilities, knowledge, organization and skills to make decisions.
Adopts a responsible, orderly attitude at work, and willingness to learn.
Knows and applies models on the structure of matter to understand the properties and behavior of substances and materials.

Knows and understands the basic principles and theories about the physical and chemical processes that different types of chemical substances can undergo under certain conditions to determine, in each application, the effects produced.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction: Chemistry's place in science, terminology, vocabulary, and basic ideas describing matter and energy behavior.

Topic 2. Electronic structure of atoms: Composition of the atom (fundamental particles), focusing on electron distribution in the atomic shell (quantum-mechanical model of electronic structure) and its relation to chemical properties and electronic configurations.

Topic 3. Periodic classification of elements: Classification of elements based on periodicity of chemical properties, highlighting ionization energy, electron affinity, and electronegativity. Justification of ionic and covalent valences of representative elements through their position in the Periodic Table.

Topic 4. Chemical Bonding: Forces holding atoms in molecules and ions in ionic compounds. Study of the three basic types of chemical bonds (ionic, covalent, and metallic) and their associated properties.

Topic 5. Intermolecular Forces. States of Aggregation of Matter: Description of weaker forces acting between molecules, and between ions and molecules (intermolecular forces) and their derived properties. Examination of the structure of the three states of matter (solid, liquid, and gas) and their common and important properties; study of main crystal types.
Topic 6. Phase Equilibria: Study of phase changes or transitions between gases, liquids, and solids based on phase diagrams.

Topic 7. Mixtures and Solutions. Properties of Solutions. Properties of Colloids and Emulsions: Study of different types of dispersed systems. In-depth study of true solutions, their magnitudes, and governing laws. Colligative properties of solutions (electrolyte solutions). Study of colloidal dispersions and their most important technical applications.
Topic 8. Thermochemistry. Combustion: Basic study of thermodynamic magnitudes and functions, and their main relationships; special attention to combustion processes.

Topic 9. Acids, Bases, and Salts: Study of acid and base definitions, pH scale, and the relationship between acid strength and molecular structure. Quantitative treatment of acid and base ionization in water.

Topic 10. Electrochemistry. Metal Corrosion: Study of electron transfer reactions in aqueous solutions (redox reactions), and interconversion processes between chemical and electrical energy. Analysis of metal corrosion by salts in aqueous solutions, its causes, and prevention.
Topic 11. Inorganic Chemistry of Industrial Interest: Synthesis, properties, and applications of the most important inorganic compounds from an industrial perspective.

Topic 12. Organic Chemistry. Polymers: Definition of organic chemistry, understanding its distinctive aspects based on the specific structure of organic molecules; study of main organic functions and their properties. Analysis of general properties of organic polymers.
assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation includes a 30% partial exam in January and a 40% (second part) or 70% (whole subject) final exam in May, complemented by 30% for laboratory practices and tasks; both the exam and lab components must be approved. Students may opt for a final evaluation consisting of an 80% written exam and a 20% specific lab and presentation test. The extraordinary call features an 80% written exam and a 20% specific lab and presentation test; continuous evaluation students may choose to retain their 30% lab and task grade, making the written exam worth 70%. Non-attendance to the written exam results in a 'Not Presented' grade.
